correctness.rationale: The free-amalgamation age realizes all compatible four-state extension words. Each forbidden rainbow triangle corresponds exactly to one of two symmetric off-diagonal zeros in \(T_c\) across an old path edge. The sorted nonzero deficits obey \(S'=2S+a+b\) and \((d'_1,d'_2,d'_3)=(S+a+b,2S+a,2S+b)\), monotone in all entries, giving all-order extrema by induction. The unique strict choices after the initial ties force monochromatic maxima and 123-periodic minima. Perron growth and finite verifier arithmetic checked. Direct finite enumeration supports but is not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: An exact model-theoretic extension complexity invariant is optimized over all \(3^{n-1}\) coloured path bases for every order \(n\), with every equality case proved. The extremal colour patterns are structurally different, and their counts have strictly separated exponential rates. The ordered-deficit comparison is a reusable method for simultaneous bounds on an entire matrix-product family, beyond a routine computation of a fixed matrix power.
